//: Not a package. A resolution redirect, so that `@rebasepro/server/functions`
works under TypeScript's legacy `moduleResolution: "node"` as well as under
The `exports` map in ../package.json is the real declaration, and it is what
Node uses at runtime — once a package has `exports`, Node ignores directory
redirects like this one entirely. TypeScript's node10 mode does the opposite:
it ignores `exports` and resolves subpaths as directories. A project scaffolded
by `rebase init` compiles with `moduleResolution: "node"`, so without this file
the very import the template ships — `@rebasepro/server/functions` — fails its
own `tsc` with TS2307, while running perfectly.
Deleting this file breaks type-checking for every such project and nothing
else, which is the hardest kind of breakage to attribute. `files` in
../package.json ships it; assert-build-output.mjs verifies the targets exist.
